teach.goal: Ponte português → inglês com palavras úteis.
solo: Peça uma frase pessoal com 2 das palavras.
group: Palavras: deadline, delay, contract, approval, budget, reminder.
Aluno diz em português um uso real, depois a palavra em inglês.
extra90: Cada aluno escolhe a palavra mais útil e explica por quê.

facts.label: Preposição + relativo
facts.sub: Pessoa: to / with / for + whom. Coisa: in / on / under + which. Formal: antes. Informal: no fim. Nunca who ou that.

facts.label: Quem
facts.sub: Use preposition + whom para pessoas em estilo formal: the people to whom I spoke. Depois de preposição, não use who. Na fala do dia a dia, a preposição vai para o fim: the people I spoke to.

facts.label: O qual
facts.sub: Use preposition + which para coisas: the room in which we met, the project on which we depend. Nunca use that depois de preposição. Em inglês informal: the room we met in.

items.s: We say “the people to who I spoke”.

answers: To whom is formal. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “the people to who I spoke”. → Falso (We say to whom.)
For things, we use preposition + which. → Verdadeiro (Yes: in which, on which.)

pages.title: A delay in an Edinburgh office · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Monday morning in a busy Edinburgh office. Rain taps on the old stone windows. Nell has just finished a difficult phone call. Her colleague Sara works at the next desk. The project they care about may be late. They need a clear plan before lunch.

“Sara, the people to whom I spoke yesterday say the project, on which we depend, may be delayed.” says Nell. “That is worrying. Who are the colleagues with whom you discussed it?” says Sara. “Mainly Hugh, for whom the deadline is a priority, and two engineers from the department in which I started.” says Nell.
